rows.subtopic: A power cut or rain spoils plans
rows.subtype: Approach: rescheduling with friends by phone [Action]
rows.description: After the trip to the mela is cancelled due to rain, a boy calls friends and suggests the next Sunday, settling on a new time before the excitement fades.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: commitment device

rows.subtype: Approach: finishing homework first, then playing [Action]
rows.description: A boy makes a rule that games start only after homework, and finds that with work done he enjoys the game more without worry in the back of his mind.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, forward planning, negotiation, prioritising, seeking advice, time-boxing

rows.description: A girl sets a timer for forty minutes of gaming on weekdays, and when it rings she stops, making the limit feel like her own rule rather than a parent's.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, forward planning, negotiation, prioritising, seeking advice

rows.description: A child tells himself only one more round, then another, and suddenly it is ten p.m. with unfinished maths, showing how a fun activity without a stopping point expands.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, forward planning, negotiation, prioritising, seeking advice, time-boxing

rows.subtype: Approach: weighing what matters more this week [Thinking]
rows.description: Knowing a test is on Friday, a boy decides that studying is more important now and games can wait for the weekend, thinking in terms of what is urgent and what can be delayed.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, forward planning, negotiation, seeking advice, time-boxing

rows.subtype: Approach: negotiating a fair deal with parents [Action]
rows.description: A girl proposes an hour of gaming on Saturday and Sunday if she keeps her weekday study plan, and her parents agree to try it for a month.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, forward planning, prioritising, seeking advice, time-boxing

rows.subtype: Approach: hiding the game and lying about homework [Pitfall]
rows.description: A boy says the homework is done and plays secretly, and when the teacher reports missing work, he faces both the marks problem and the lost trust.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: forward planning, negotiation, prioritising, seeking advice, time-boxing

rows.subtype: Approach: using the game as a reward for goals [Thinking]
rows.description: A child decides that after finishing two chapters she earns thirty minutes of her game, turning it into a motivator rather than a competitor for time.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, forward planning, negotiation, prioritising, seeking advice, time-boxing

rows.subtype: Approach: noticing tiredness and changing the routine [Revision]
rows.description: After falling asleep in class from late gaming, the boy realises the cost, moves gaming to the afternoon and puts the console away by nine at night.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, negotiation, prioritising, seeking advice, time-boxing

rows.subtype: Approach: playing a game with friends instead of alone [Thinking]
rows.description: A girl finds the pull to play alone is strong, so she decides to play only when her cousins are around, which limits time and adds fun in a natural way.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, forward planning, negotiation, prioritising, seeking advice, time-boxing
